newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sameco aluminium output down - agency.
newsitem.headline: Sameco aluminium output down - agency.

text.p: Rolled aluminium output at Russia's Samara Metals Co (Sameco) was 41,600 tonnes in the first seven months of this year, a drop of 46 percent on year-ago levels, Interfax news agency said on Friday.

It quoted deputy chief executive Vladimir Mukhin as saying AO Samarskaya Metallurgicheskaya Kompaniya planned to produce 50,300 tonnes of rolled aluminium from August to December and that planned production for 1996 had been 160,000 tonnes.
Mukhin was quoted as saying unprofitable export and decreased domestic rolled aluminium demand were responsible for falling production.
Mukhin declined by telephone to comment on 1996 output but told Reuters 1995 rolled aluminium output was 154,000 tonnes.
Rolled aluminium is Sameco's primary product, and makes up 85-90 percent of production.
Sameco produces a number of aluminium products except foil, he said. It is not a primary aluminium producer.

Sameco's board of directors is considering joining the Siberian Aluminium financial industrial group including Bratsk Aluminium, Sayansk Aluminium, London-based Trans World Metals Group and Kazakhstan's Pavlodar Aluminium, which produces alumina, not aluminium.
Mukhin said he expected his board to make a decision on Sameco's strategic course in September. "There are a number of other alliance possibilities," he said.
He said Sameco may work more closely with Bratsk Aluminium, but there were no negotiations on direct investment by Bratsk in Sameco.

"We have a long and good relationship with Bratsk," he said. Sameco could work with Bratsk through Siberian Aluminium or simply agree on primary aluminium supply contracts if they could agree on a price.
